But Herodorus (31 fr. 31 J.) and Euphorion in the Xenios (fr. 35 Scheidw.) say that Cerberus was brought up there by Heracles and vomited bile, from which grew the plant called aconite. Andron of Teos in the Periplus (fr. 1 M. II 348) says that a certain Acheron ruled over the region, whose daughter was Dardanis; when Heracles had intercourse with her, she had a son called Poimen; and when Dardanis and her son Poimen died at the same time, the places were named after them, Dardanis and Poimen, in the territory of Heraclea.
c. He says it stretches on high, that is, it is lofty. P

d. And eddying Acheron: the river Acheron flows into the sea through a great ravine, cutting through the Acherusian headland. For near Heraclea in the land of the Mariandyni there is a river Acheron and a cavernous mouth. 'Ravine' means the ruggedness of the mountain and a mountain hollow; for a ravine is a mountain hollow.
357-59a. Near to it: to the land of the Mariandyni. The order is: close by the land of the Mariandyni you sail past the mountains of the Paphlagonians.
c. And to them Enetian: from Enete, a city of the Paphlagonians. Homer (B 852): 'from the Eneti, whence the race of mules'. These they called Caucones
before the Trojan War. He said Pelops was Paphlagonian by birth, but others record that he was Lydian; Euphorion (fr. 135 Scheidw.) agrees with both opinions.
d. 〈steadfast in battle:〉 it is written Enetian. Lg Gm
e. The phrase 'and although they boast to be of his blood' has the 'per' as redundant; for the Paphlagonians said they were descended from Pelops. P

360-63a. There is a headland of Helice: that the Carambis headland is high and precipitous in Paphlagonia and stretches into the sea toward the north, Ephorus also mentions in book 4 (70 fr. 41 J.). The sense: there is a headland and high projection stretching into the sea, lying opposite the Bear of Helice, by which the blasts of Boreas are split, that is, the winds. It is a hyperbaton, and 'hypo' is used for 'hyper': by which the blasts of Boreas are split.

b. Perhaps it is better to take 'hyper' as 'above': above Carambis the blasts of Boreas are split or dispersed. For if on the peaks of high mountains there is calm, as the natural philosophers claim, much more so above them. Therefore he adds: so turned toward the sea it reaches and approaches the aether. P
c. 〈reaches the aether:〉 Carambis approaches the aether. Lg
